nodes.label: Honesty point: complementarity/selectivity — which molecular partners bind, a...
nodes.statement: Honesty point: complementarity/selectivity — which molecular partners bind, and why not others — is the paper's organizing principle for why this hierarchy assembles, but it is not a mechanism this executable implements or tests. Every handler reads and writes a fixed, pre-declared store path; there is no binding-affinity calculation, no competing partner, and no non-cognate binder that gets rejected. What is demonstrated is hierarchical assembly (a six-level nested place graph that compiles, resolves every leaf, and carries coupled dynamics from its deepest node outward), not fitted binding selectivity. This study does not claim a selectivity mechanism that was not built.

Two distinct idioms answer "can development/evolution be a compositional rewr...
nodes.statement: Two distinct idioms answer "can development/evolution be a compositional rewrite?" differently, and they should not be conflated. The compiled/executable path (fig10-2-executable, fig10-3-executable) uses ordinary Process handlers behind a preserved interface — no place-graph rewrite occurs there. A separate Live-Topology pair (fig10-2-rewrite, fig10-3-rewrite) genuinely inserts and removes place-graph nodes at runtime via an `overwrite[tree[node]]` output (biofilm colonization to capacity 5 then ECM secretion per cell; a mutant lineage sweep that prunes the wildtype to zero) — closer in spirit to Fig 10-1's division rewrite, but driven by a fixed wall-clock schedule and a hardcoded mutant fitness advantage (1.6), not by the community's own state.
